children: have ended a long-running legal battle over technology used in Lululemon’s Mirror home fitness platform, according to a filing in Manhattan federal court.

The companies jointly notified the court Wednesday that they had agreed to dismiss the lawsuit with prejudice, preventing the same claims from being brought again. The filing did not disclose whether the companies reached a settlement.

brought the case in 2022, claiming that Mirror’s technology violated six of its patents. The patents covered functions including controlling workout intensity, allowing users to compete, and tracking exercise performance through fitness equipment and smartphone applications.

contested the allegations and subsequently challenged the patents before a U.S. Patent and Trademark Office tribunal. Proceedings in the federal case were put on hold in 2023. The tribunal later invalidated relevant portions of five of the six patents, while Nike
earlier this year lost appeals involving two of the tribunal’s decisions.
purchased Mirror for about $453 million in July 2020. The company offered an interactive home workout platform with live and on-demand classes.
The case was Nike, Inc. v. Lululemon Athletica, Inc. et al. in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

title: Nike, Lululemon drop patent case tied to Mirror home gym
